text: Energy Bandwidth Study of 2006 and also the 2015 update were reviewed. Detailed conversations with industry representatives (APPTI) were performed to accommodate the impact on the balance of plant alterations to paper drying processes. A comprehensive literature review 35 DE-EE0009395 was conducted to define baseline performance benchmarking of paper drying, including energy and cost performance. This review is based on a broad range of official reports, especially DOE reports and published academic papers. The original DOE energy bandwidth study of the pulp and paper industry was carried out in 2006 and updated in 2015. They provide data for individual sections and products for the papermaking process. The drying paper's current typical energy intensity estimation was selected as a baseline to estimate potential energy savings for three paper types relative to baselines. The project team determined to use the linerboard, fluted corrugating medium, and white (bleached) containerboard since they are within 18.6% of the total energy consumption of the entire range of paper and paperboard types, which is reasonable for a modeling exercise. These three products also represent about 45% of the U.S. paper market, which could lead to the most impactful energy efficiency improvements if the industry implements them. The process model was developed considering the steam-condensate and air ventilation systems. Typical multi-cylinder dryer section of paper machine The accuracy of the developed process model was validated against data that was obtained from available industrial reports and literature. The validation of the process model was carried out using the actual paper machine-linerboard data for 2019. The paper drying process within the machine consists of the main (pre-drying) and after-drying sections. The drying process consists of 75 dryer cylinders that are 72-inch diameter. The steam system is a hybrid cascade thermo- compressor system. The complexity of moisture introduction with the sizing section and air dryer percentage of drying has been considered. The steam-condensate system consists of a cylinder block, steam-water separation block, and condensation block. The ventilation system consists of a hood block, heat recovery block, supply air heating block, and fan block. The basic input data of the dryer process was compiled from the industrial report, including machine speed, basis weight, sheet width, press moisture, moisture into size press, size press moisture, starch solids, and pickup and steam pressure.
